To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) seven rat monoclonal antibody for bovine myoglobins were produced, (ii) five antibodies reacted with surface absorbed myoglobin whereas the remaining two reacted only in a two-site sandwich ELISA, and (iii) a two-site sandwich enzyme immunoassays was developed and allowed the quantification of 0.03 ng/ml bovine Myoglobin.

(i) the seven monoclonal antibodies for bovine myoglobins were able to detect the protein in a sandwich type immunoassay and to discriminate between the two major forms of the protein, (ii) the antibodies were able to detect myoglobin in serum and urine from animals suffering from myopathy, and (iii) the two-site immunoassay allowed quantification of myoglobin in serum with a lower limit of detection of 30 ng/mL.
seven monoclonal antibodies for bovine myoglobins were produced, three of them were noncompeting and could be used in a two-site immunoassay to quantitatively determine myoglobin in serum and urine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a sensitive immunoassay for the quantification of myoglobin in the blood and urine of animals.
the development of a sensitive, rapid and specific enzyme immunoassays for the quantification of bovines myoglobin in urine and serum.
the production and characterization of monoclonal antibodies for myoglobin, a protein which is of great importance in veterinary medicine and in clinical diagnosis of myocardial infarction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

these seven MAbs recognize seven epitope regions on bovine myoglobin and that the antibodies can be applied in the quantitative determination of bovine myoglobulin in serum and urine.
